newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ BANKER RICHWHITE PLEASED WITH WINEBOX OUTCOME.
newsitem.headline: NZ BANKER RICHWHITE PLEASED WITH WINEBOX OUTCOME.

text.p: Fay, Richwhite principal David Richwhite said on Thursday he was pleased Sir Ronald Davison's tax inquiry had cleared the merchant bank of any wrongdoing.

Davison's commission report concluded that neither the Inland Revenue (IRD) nor the Serious Fraud Office (SFO) were guilty of any wrongdoing involving the so called "winebox" of tax transaction documents at the heart of his investigation.
Fay, Richwhite's name came up several times during the inquiry into tax deals done in the late 1980s and involving a number of New Zealand and foreign corporates.
In reporting its conclusions after nearly three years' work, the inquiry also concluded those deals were not fraudulent.
The winebox inquiry was instigated by then MP Winston Peters -- now treasurer and deputy prime minister.
"It has been a long and difficult process that started back in 1992 when Winston Peters first made his attacks under parliamentary privilege," Richwhite said in a statement.
"The report concludes that there was no basis whatsoever for those attacks," he said.
Davison noted in his report that it was not possible for anyone to take action against Peters for his allegations, because he made them under parliamentary privilege.
"However, he notes that the findings of this commission may go some way to remedying the injustices done," Richwhite said.
"With this inquiry finished and the report released, the individuals, companies and organisations concerned can now move on to more positive and productive activity," Richwhite said.
